title.narrative: Advancing Ethical and Human Rights-Based Climate Technology Governance in Pacific SIDS

description.narrative: This work plan aims to support Pacific Member States in developing and implementing ethical and human rights-based frameworks for frontier and digital technologies, with a strong focus on climate action. Pacific SIDS are at the frontline of climate change, facing rising sea levels, extreme weather events, and environmental degradation. At the same time, emerging technologies—including AI, biotechnology, and climate-related innovations—offer significant opportunities for adaptation, mitigation, and resilience-building. However, without ethical safeguards, these technologies may exacerbate inequalities, undermine rights, or fail to respond to local priorities. Building on UNESCO’s normative instruments, including the Declaration of Ethical Principles in Relation to Climate Change and guidance from IBC and COMEST, this work plan will support Member States in integrating ethical considerations into climate-related science and technology policies. It will promote responsible innovation that aligns with human rights, gender equality, and sustainability, while ensuring that climate solutions are inclusive and context-appropriate. The rationale is to address gaps in the governance of emerging technologies in climate action, including limited institutional capacities, lack of ethical guidance, and insufficient integration of human rights principles in policy frameworks. By strengthening ethical governance, enhancing policy capacities, and fostering partnerships, UNESCO will support Pacific Member States in leveraging technology for climate resilience while safeguarding societal values and long-term sustainability.
